chapter: Small group, new sound and Europe
title: Marshall Royal and discipline in the rebuilt band
summary: Greene agrees the band of 1952 had a different character, with Marshall Royal as bandmaster.

story.theme_name: Playing with Count Basie: joining, leading, leaving
story.community_name: Playing with Count Basie: the band, its feel and its people

blocks.x: You can't quite rely on this because it's just records.
Uh-huh.
Seems to me it goes from 1950 ---
I know it's 1950. I know that.
-- to sort of '51.
Mm hmm.
Yeah, it says 'except for a period in 1950-51 --

The point seems to me, Freddie, that from 1937 up until the time of the break up, you know, the small group -- that was more or less the same policy. Personnel changed so that the band sounds a bit different, but when the band is formed again with Marshall Royal in '52, it seems to have a different character. Would you agree with that?
I think so. I think you could say that, yeah.
Who would you hold responsible for that, Marshall?
Well, Marshall -- I would say Marshall partially because of the fact that he was like the bandmaster, more or less, you know.
Yeah.

He kept everything going musically, and Basie let him take charge of the band as far as directing the band, and what-not. And, I think he has an awful lot of influence as far as the sound is concerned.
So, Freddie, there was more discipline introduced into the band in a sense then, would you say?
Yeah. Musically, yes, I think so.
As far as rehearsals --
Yes.
-- as far as standards --
Definitely. Definitely.
-- yeah.
